Results.ReviewText: We pre-ordered the Timberline 1300 and arrived last October from our local store.  The first 3 months of use were awesome. But after using it time after time, grease started to accumulate in between the wall where the grease drips down into the tray and BAM, our 1st fire happened. This is our 4th Traeger grill so we know how to clean and use them.  We have been customers for over 8 years and absolutely love the taste of our food. We have upgraded about very 2-3 years. We clean our Traeger about every 14 days as we use it almost everyday, except the past week. We had our 4th fire in this model and had to use the fire extinguisher this time. After the 3rd fire about 6 weeks ago, the CS person from traeger was the only helpful one that sent us new parts and we had uploaded picture of the fire and inside of the Timberline 1300 and discovered the tray and liner on the bottom of grill had warped. We replaced those parts and terminally cleaned the grill and cooked steaks on it once. Started the grill about a week ago to cook hamburgers and when it reached 320 degrees, BAM our 4th fire. I have called traeger customer service 3 times and my husband has called twice and we can not get anyone to help us! Now I have a $2000 paper weight on my patio and feel this model is poorly designed. So I would be very cautious before buying the Timberline model.
Results.Title: Do not buy!

Results.ReviewText:
I have been a Traeger fan for years, not my first Traeger, and I have loved all the fun cookout times that I have had.

I bought this grill during the original release, I got in line and felt fortunate enough to get one within a few weeks of the original shipping date.

I have worked in embedded systems development for years, and I got about what I expected when I saw a grill company trying to design an internet of things device, quite a steep learning curve on the part of Traeger, and a lot of patience from me.

I had a unit replaced because of an inexplicable blower fan error. I had a board replaced because the wifi antenna that they designed into it does not have sufficient positive lock and it came loose in shipping. I put up with all of the tunings and retunings of the PID control of the system, either causing the thing to spew smoke for the whole cook, or go out, or backup. I learned to dread the next firmware update, and what new quirks it was going to bring. 

A year or so in and I worked through all those issues with Traegers help, much happier now that so many of the firmware bugs were getting resolved, it has been more reliable, and I loved that I could program up my cooks and start them at night and wake up in the morning and expect it to be doing exactly the right thing at the right time. These were fantastic times, and I finally started feeling like I was getting what I paid for. 

Then the updates started to get worse. Unannounced database updates making it so my unit wouldn't show up without an app update, obfuscation of the only part of the app that I care about which is to control my grill, nonsensical "improvements" to the UI on the phone just making it harder to do what I needed to do.

Now with the latest app update I can't see my carefully curated custom cook cycles unless i use the manual interface on the front of the grill, and I don't believe that i can trust that to be there the next time I power it on and get an OTA update.

I'm one firmware update away from selling this thing and getting something else. 

I've been a die hard traeger fan since I first started but they are making it really hard to stay that way. I still appreciate the patience and responsiveness of their dealers and customer support, but man the app is terrible, and I feel like I am at the mercy of the firmware update schedule. For a top of the line product, this was anything other than a top of the line experience.
Results.Title: Not what was promised

Results.ReviewText:
We just purchased our second Timberline 1300.  This one is for vacation home in southern Utah.  FedEx dropped it off just before noon.  My son and I spent less than an hour assembling it.  Really, the instructions are so well written and the parts are all numbered.  Even the bolts and nuts are separated into phases of assembly.  That evening we smoked chicken.  The next evening we had pork ribs and smoked cauliflower.  Sunday was beef brisket and burnt ends.  I think we got it pretty well seasoned.  We didn't do any reverse searing this last week but steak will never be the same once you try it on a Traeger.  

The double wall insulation of not only the side walls but also the door make this pretty stingy with the fuel.  The Wifire technology makes it so I could even take in 9 holes of golf while I was cooking dinner.  If the cooking is moving too slowly, just turn up the heat from the golf course with the Traeger App on your phone.  If you can't get back soon enough just turn the temperature to "keep warm".  

The Timberline is the perfect blend of the old art of smoking with modern double walled construction and digital technology.  I LOVE wifire technology!   The Timberline 1300 boasts enough room to cook multiple courses for a large family with very efficient fuel consumption.  The best compliment I could give would be:  Six racks of baby backs - All gone!  18lb full packer brisket - All gone!  Compliments - Still flowing!  I'm not just blowing smoke up your Traeger!  

As for the son who helped with assembly, he will be moving into a new home this fall.  Guess what he wants for a housewarming gift.  His brother has a Timberline 1300 just waiting in the garage to welcome him to the Traegerhood!
Results.Title: Old Methods Collide with Technology

Customer service has been really good as far as getting me new parts. However the person helping me said they can’t do anything about the peeling paint. And they said she would put It in my account we will see if anything happens So at this point if I was still in the time frame to return for a refund I sure would. Results.ReviewText: It is a great unit especially for the colder areas in climate. Traeger got fancy and created a design flaw for the grease bucket and should have kept it simple. There is a drawer style trap with a cover connecting to the rope seal underneath the grill. Thinking great idea? Not so much. Unless you want grease all over the ground where your grill sits. The rope seal traps all that grease and runs it along the top plate cover spilling it out the sides of the drawer. Take the Top plate off and you will be fine.

Results.ReviewText: I purchased a new Pro 575 last July 2019. Bought the cover & shelf etc. Read the manual and attempted to use. Out of the first half dozen times I attempted to use it, I was successful maybe once. I would set the temperature and ignite. Next thing I know, I come back and it has overheated and is shutting down. If it did pre-heat properly, any adjusting of the temperature during cooking causes another overheat and shutdown. I even a had a fire in the hopper. Eventually I was sent a new control panel which I installed. It seemed to work the first few times but I continue to have problems. Last weekend I decided to try a beef roast. Got the recipe from Traeger and set the temp at 200. Put my roast in and come back to check on it a short time later. Temp is 300. I open the lid to cool it down, give it 15-20 minutes and come back. Now the temp is 150 and going down. It is still set at  200. How in heck do you cook with that. The new control high temp limit is only 450 degrees. In my opinion that does not sear a steak. The first panel had a high limit of 550 degrees. I am very disappointed and beyond mad!
Results.Title: not happy

Results.ReviewText: The Timberline 1300 is one heck of a smoker. We use it 3-5 times a week for just about anything we want to cook. Brisket, steaks, pork shoulder, fish, pizzas, bread, veggies, cookies, it does it all and makes everything taste awesome with that wood fired flavor. Results.ReviewText:
Observations:

1. Your front tray is useless - Extend it another 4-6" or fit for purpose
2. Turn pellet top and wood board sideways so functional
3. Look at second grill grate from bottom - if left inside cannot turn food from bottom grill grate
4. When Super Smoke is turned on leave words on screen - "Super Smoke On"
5. Fix heat seals under hood and around grill better - Snaps come loose too much
6. Make WiFI easier - Why 2G and not normal house WIFI? Hassle to align up
7. Your accessories need some work - Spatula is good but tongs are way to stiff - Really not functional as designed
8. Fix placement of grease bucket - To get out you always spill grease - Straight in and straight out no need to tilt to get out
9. Hire design people who ask questions as if "they" we cooking - Not a bad idea

Results.ReviewText: I got my smoker a lil over a month ago 350lb to say it’s well built is an understatement. Got everything together and did the first burn in everything going smooth. Decided to hook up WiFi and this is where It goes south. Get the newest update installed and boom stops working. Tried hooking up to two different devices with no luck. Not a big deal it’s a know issue it’ll get taken care of quickly right...wrong. Called support and after an hr on the phone trying everything it still doesn’t work no Big deal they’ll send a new one out. It’s been over 4 weeks and haven’t received anything so I call back and apparently the first guy didn’t write notes so now we have to go through everything again to make sure it’s not working. I work out of town and I’m only home a week at a time some now it’s going to be at least another month before I fully get to enjoy this expansion smoker. So in short if you want a well built smoker it’s worth It but if you want It for the wifi I’d reconsider.

Results.ReviewText:
The quality of this grill is the highest that I have seen. I am a contractor and have seen all brands/types of grills place in the summer kitchens and none have compared to the Timberline 1300.The body is solid and stable. The grates are heavy and well made. Assembly was almost seamless...due to the weight, I would definitely suggest an extra helper. The interface is self intuitive and easy to use.
Up to date, I have smoke a meatloaf (directly on rack), (2) Boston Butts and ribeyes (smoked and then reverse seared). All have turned out perfect, the meat loaf was a first for me and honestly it was the best meat loaf I have ever tasted. The pork had a great flavor and pulled with ease. The steaks had the perfect amount of smoke and were exceptionally tender. The reverse sear worked well on the steaks. This grill will reach a temp of 500+ degrees, which was my only real concern about ordering this type of grill. I would recommend this grill to anyone looking for the perfect all-around high quality smoker/grill.
